report_name: North Korean APT Kimsuky Linked to "Trigram" Espionage Campaign

threat_actors.name: Kimsuky
threat_actors.description: North Korean APT group conducting the 'Trigram' cyber-espionage campaign, targeting AI, blockchain, and logistics sectors in Europe and the U.S. using social engineering with fake job offers.
threat_actors.goals: Intelligence gathering and revenue generation from technology sectors.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: The attack begins with a personalized email to a target, such as a software developer, containing a link to a fake job opportunity.

attack_patterns.name: Malicious Link
attack_patterns.description: After a fake verification step on an attacker-controlled platform, the victim is directed to click a link that delivers the malicious payload.

attack_patterns.name: Credentials from Password Stores
attack_patterns.description: The OverLord infostealer harvests credentials from browsers, email clients, and other applications on the victim's system.

attack_patterns.name: Employee Names
attack_patterns.description: Attackers identify and target specific software developers with personalized emails and fake job offers as part of their social engineering efforts.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing via Service
attack_patterns.description: Attackers impersonate recruiters from up to 50 different companies, using fake job offers to lure victims via email.

attack_patterns.name: PowerShell
attack_patterns.description: PowerShell is likely used for execution after the initial payload, as indicated by hunting hints to monitor its execution from downloaded files or email links.

attack_patterns.name: Visual Basic
attack_patterns.description: The use of malicious .LNK files as an initial payload suggests that scripting, potentially VBScript, is used for execution.

malware.name: OverLord
malware.description: An information-stealing malware delivered as the final payload in the Trigram campaign to harvest credentials and sensitive documents.

campaigns.name: Trigram
campaigns.description: A cyber-espionage campaign attributed to Kimsuky targeting AI, blockchain, and logistics sectors in Europe and the U.S. using fake job offers to deliver information-stealing malware.
campaigns.objective: Deployment of information-stealing malware to gather intelligence and potentially generate revenue.

identities.name: Artificial Intelligence Sector
identities.description: Organizations in the AI sector in Europe and the U.S. were targeted by the Kimsuky Trigram campaign.

identities.name: Blockchain Sector
identities.description: Organizations in the blockchain sector in Europe and the U.S. were targeted by the Kimsuky Trigram campaign.

identities.name: Logistics Sector
identities.description: Organizations in the logistics sector in Europe and the U.S. were targeted by the Kimsuky Trigram campaign.

infrastructure.name: Kimsuky Victim Management Platform
infrastructure.description: A sophisticated web platform controlled by Kimsuky to manage the operation, track victims through the infection process, and deliver the payload.

infrastructure.name: Kimsuky Payload and Exfiltration Server
infrastructure.description: An attacker-controlled server used to deliver the OverLord infostealer payload and receive exfiltrated data.

indicators.name: Kimsuky Trigram Lure Files
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Kimsuky Trigram Campaign Lure File Creation
id: 938b1f2e-a4c1-4d5e-8f6a-7b8c9d0e1f2a
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of lure files with names used in the Kimsuky Trigram campaign.
references:
  - https://www.stormshield.com/news/cti-trigram-campaign/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-11
tags:
  - attack.t1566.002
  - attack.t1204.001
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\Job_Description.lnk'
      - '\Coding_Challenge.zip'
  condition: selection

indicators.name: Suspicious PowerShell Execution from Phishing Lure
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious PowerShell Execution from Phishing Lure
id: 5e8f6a7b-8c9d-4e1f-a2b3-c4d5e6f7a8b9
status: experimental
description: Detects PowerShell being launched by a browser or email client, a common TTP in phishing campaigns like Kimsuky's Trigram.
references:
  - https://www.stormshield.com/news/cti-trigram-campaign/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-11
tags:
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.execution
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\outlook.exe'
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\iexplore.exe'
  condition: all of selection_*
